![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/3fe3ec24f8f8006f22bde8ba2dc39fd3cd3f73668b06f8ea4a74e4ed5206a193.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the front one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/2a20f2651c24e48871028b44fe61da4600d632481877ef32ccdfd3241262a53b.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type II region

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le 5-y-\frac{z}{2}\},
$$

where

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 4\}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/1ba7c02f254313a73a813e4e43c44c25523ce77dd47e594a1db3b412a6bd5c3d.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 3,\,\,0\le z\le 4,\,\,0\le x\le 5-y-\frac{z}{2}\}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{5-y-z/2}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}\,dx\,dz\,dy.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{5-y-z/2}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}\,dx\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{5-y-z/2}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}\,dx]dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}[x]_{x=0}^{x=5-y-z/2}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{10-2y-z}(5-y-\frac{z}{2})\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{2}\,dz\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{2}\,dz\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{2}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[\frac{z}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=4}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}2\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}2\,dy & =[2y]_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =6-0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
